free_tier.stated: Korean government programmes give Rebellions ATOM accelerators away, and the channel is a company. A published technical account states: 'K-Cloud Project (MSIT and NIPA, 3 years from 2023): the AI Semiconductor Farm construction and demonstration program. Three CSPs (Naver Cloud, KT Cloud, NHN Cloud) and three AI-chip makers (Rebellions, Sapeon, FuriosaAI) form a consortium' and 'High-Performance Computing Support Program (MSIT and NIPA, about 16.7B KRW in 2026): provides domestic NPU servers free of charge to selected demand companies... Gabia, for instance, provides Rebellions ATOM-Max at no cost.' The authors obtained '4x ATOM+ cards through one of these paths, in the form of KT Cloud's AI Nexus'.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The four cards arrived inside KT Cloud's AI Nexus, a rented cloud account with government funding behind it, and the compiler on top is free. It does not chain for a non-Korean individual: the free path exists only as a selection decision.

limits.value: allocation is by selection as a demand company inside a national programme, so the gate is a legal entity in Korea plus a review, not a quota.

identity_cost.detail: a company selected into a Korean government programme, not an individual signup: capacity goes to 'selected demand companies', and the one documented route to hardware is '4x ATOM+ cards through one of these paths, in the form of KT Cloud's AI Nexus', a rented cloud account. What the KT Cloud account itself requires (a card, a Korean phone number, a business registration number) is not stated in this record's evidence, and no hold, debit or prepaid term is stated.

evidence.proved: published 2026-07-07: both programme descriptions, 'about 16.7B KRW in 2026', and 'We too obtained 4x ATOM+ cards through one of these paths, in the form of KT Cloud's AI Nexus', all quoted
KT Cloud launched an NPU Server on Rebellions chips for public institutions, the first Korean NPUaaS provider with CSAP certification
the RBLN SDK, compiler, runtime and a 300-model zoo are published for developers at no stated price

notes: This is the largest free accelerator allocation that is not a trial, and it is unreachable for the reason every national allocation is. Confidence is reported because the primary sources are programme notices plus one operator account; What would settle it: the 2026 NIPA notice text and its applicant class.
